_comment: Experiment 2: is 64 segments too many? 64 piecewise-constant controls x 3 = 192 free values fitting 64 position points leaves room for a path that threads the points on a wandering route; fewer knots make that geometrically harder. CONFOUND, stated rather than hidden: under true-time-position the supervision grid IS the segment grid (Q=N, endpoint q at true time q*T/N), so an N=16 arm also trains on 16 position points instead of 64. The two cannot be separated without changing the objective, so a positive result here means 'a coarser control AND supervision grid helps', not 'fewer controls help'. Checkpoint selection is unaffected: validation_common_grid_points stays 64 for every arm, so the selector compares like with like, and score_control_arms.py resamples every arm onto one 64-point grid.
